audit.whatIsWrong: Page frames the lane as an "even poke war" and the level chart is entirely "Skill", while the data says Neeko 71.93% over 57 games and the packet chart reads Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Neeko/Azir/Azir. The content layer win[] already reads Neeko x5 then Azir x2, so the full layer contradicts the content layer on every row.
audit.why: Azir's level 1-2 pattern is two Sand Soldiers with Conquering Sands on a 14s cooldown at rank 1; he has no trade back at melee-adjacent range. Neeko's E is a 12s root at 1000 range into a Q that blooms again on champion hit. Post-Nashor's, three soldiers plus attack speed out-range and out-DPS her.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-4 to Neeko (matching win[]), rows 5-6 to Azir, with rows 5-6 whys rewritten to describe Azir winning those stages.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes ended on "Luden's makes the package lethal" and phases[5]/[6] both credited Neeko, ignoring that Azir's Nashor's Tooth timing is the spike that ends her window.
audit.why: The content layer already identifies Nashor's plus three soldiers as the flip point (spikes[2], whys[5]). The full layer never says it.
audit.corrected: Level 3 root-bloom is the kill pattern; level 6 adds the ambush; his Nashor's ends your window.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive R-vs-R interaction was never stated: Emperor's Divide is a knockback wall of soldiers, and it is the tool that denies Neeko's Pop Blossom engage. breakdown.cooldowns also contained no digit at all (defect catalogue item 3) — it said "His shield-dash to a soldier" with no number.
audit.why: enemyKit R carries the terrain flag ("creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes") and knocks back; the missing-interactions file flags exactly this: Azir denies Pop Blossom (R) with Emperor's Divide (R). Real cooldowns from the kits: Shifting Sands 22/20.5/19/17.5/16 at 1100 range with a shield, Conquering Sands 14/12/10/8/6, Neeko E 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, both ultimates 120/105/90.
audit.corrected: Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1 and 16s maxed; step up after he burns it. Emperor's Divide knocks you back out of Pop Blossom range, so flank rather than engage down the lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no numbers (defect 3) and named no punishable window.
audit.why: Shifting Sands at 22s rank 1 is the longest relevant cooldown in the lane and is his only escape from a root.
audit.corrected: Numbers added for Shifting Sands, Conquering Sands and Neeko's E.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave was champion-agnostic template — it never mentioned that Azir's pre-Nashor's waveclear is slow.
audit.why: Two soldiers on a 1.5s summon with a 14s Conquering Sands clears slowly; shoving into him costs him farm or forces a step into E range.
audit.corrected: Wave advice rewritten around his slow two-soldier clear and soldier-range poke.
sources: enemyKit W cd 1.5 / Q cd 14 at rank 1

audit.whatIsWrong: Copy-paste bleed (defect 2): dosFull[0].d carried the cooldowns sentence, dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim — each under an unrelated title.
audit.why: Titles promise clone play and soldier-line trading; the bodies explained something else.
audit.corrected: All three bodies replaced with content matching their titles and grounded in Azir's kit.

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. It governs your forward steps. - W Shapesplitter clone spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.

edits.before: Track Azir’s Shifting Sands: His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Shifting Sands: 22s at rank 1, 16s maxed. It shields him and dashes 1100 range to a soldier — step in only once he has spent it on the wave.

edits.before: Poke blooms and tell lies — your trades are even and your information war isn't. Every clone he answers wrong is tempo.
edits.after: Two soldiers give him nothing back — walk up on every soldier last-hit, bloom him, and make level 3 a kill, not a poke exchange.

edits.before: Post-6, hunt clumps: disguise into the wave, R the river contest, root the scatter. One good crouch is a won objective.
edits.after: Post-6 his clear is still slow: shove, crouch a bush, and R him before Nashor's lands. Every minute wasted is a minute he scales.

edits.before: Best wave: a bloom-cleared push that crashes while your clone walks somewhere worth lying about — every shove is also a misdirection. Worst wave: a frozen wave near his tower with E down and the clone on cooldown — one honest Neeko is half a champion. Crash timing: every crash should buy something — a reset, a plate, a roam. Autopilot shoving buys ganks.
edits.after: Best wave: shove hard before Nashor's — two soldiers clear slowly, so he either drops farm or steps into E range. Worst wave: frozen at his tower with E down, where soldiers tax every last-hit for free. Crash timing: crash before his recall so he buys late, and never leave the wave parked at soldier range with your root on cooldown.

edits.before: If Azir takes first blood, tighten up: Shifting Sands is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with blooms and stay relevant through root picks and clone scouting.
edits.after: If Azir gets the lead he reaches Nashor's early and shoves you in — farm the bounce, treat 1100-range Shifting Sands as an escape you cannot chase, and take picks off clone scouting rather than a lane duel.

edits.before: Carry through deception — every fight you start disguised begins 5v4 in spirit; your job is the patience the crouch demands.
edits.after: Carry from side angles — Emperor's Divide only walls the line he is facing, so flank the clump it herds and drop Pop Blossom behind it.

edits.before: You are the ambush their comp can't draft against: disguise, flank, Pop Blossom on three, root the survivors. The clone scouts the setup for free.
edits.after: Never walk the lane at him — three soldiers plus Nashor's out-DPS you outright. Disguise wide, wait out Emperor's Divide, then land R on the clump it left.

edits.before: His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Every soldier last-hit puts him at 740 range with no trade back — auto, Q, and step out before Conquering Sands returns.

edits.before: E his step-up, Q the rooted target for all three blooms, auto the passive, walk — the full package is half a bar at level 3.
edits.after: Send the clone one way and walk the other — before Nashor's he cannot both shove the wave and track where you actually went.

edits.before: Azir whiffs Shifting Sands and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: E through the soldier line, then Q on top so all three blooms hit.

edits.before: That is Azir’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Your E is the kill button on a 12s cooldown — spend it on his step-up, not soldiers.

edits.before: Q-poking with E banked 'for safety' until the lane forgets your kill threat exists — the root IS the threat; the bloom is just the receipt.
edits.after: Stepping into a full three-soldier line after his Nashor's — his sustained damage beats yours there, and Shifting Sands leaves before you can answer.

notes: Level chart: full-layer phases[].side was all "Skill" while content win[] already read Neeko x5 / Azir x2, matching the packet chart and the 71.93% win rate over 57 games. Proposed the full-layer sides as one atomic group; no win[] edits were needed because the content layer was already correct. diff stays "EVEN" — the enum vocabulary in neeko.full.js is EVEN/TRICKY/HARD/MIRROR with no favourable value, so there is nothing better to move it to, and diffRating/carryRating were left alone rather than invented. Emperor's Divide is stated as a knockback that displaces Neeko out of Pop Blossom range; whether it cancels the Pop Blossom wind-up outright is not in Riot's text and was not asserted.
